_meta._comment: Read me first. Everything else in this file is app content you can edit.
_meta.name: Royal Furniture — master data
_meta.purpose: Single editable source for items, prices, categories, copy, labels, settings and test data.
_meta.harvestSource: app catalogue (1360 rows) + committed site harvest (1363 product pages, captured 2026-10-16)
_meta.placeholderRule: Any value that starts with "REPLACE_ME" is a placeholder — search the file for it, replace the value (the hint in brackets tells you what to put there) and drop the marker.
_meta.sampleRule: Records containing "_sample": true are invented examples for testing (orders, accounts). Delete or replace them.

conventions.ids: product ids are "<sku-number>-<slug>" from the feed; deal ids reuse the same scheme; store/section ids are lowercase slugs
conventions.money: integer AED amounts, rendered as "AED 1,234". All prices are what the app displays (tax-inclusive by convention).
conventions.nulls: null means "the app should not show this field"; omitted keys mean the same and keep the file small
conventions.dates: ISO "YYYY-MM-DD"; deliveryEstimate is a quoted date and goes stale — prefer deliveryDays
conventions.specs: specs[section] is a list of [label, value] pairs, section names match the website (material, dimensions, specs, warranty, assembly, size_comfort_guide)
conventions.gallery: gallery entries are paths relative to settings.images.baseUrl; image/gallery[0] is absolute

howToEdit: Edit any value, save, and the app reloads (Metro watches JSON imports).
Hide a product from the app during testing: set its "enabled": false.
Change a price: edit "price", and "listPrice" if the item has a strike-through price. Keep "discountPercent" consistent with them — that is the % OFF pill.
Add a product: copy an existing record, give it a unique "id", then add it to a category that exists in "categories".
Per-size prices live in the product's "sizes" array — the size dropdown uses these.
Unknown values are marked "REPLACE_ME" — replace them or the app shows nothing for that field.

sectionGuide.controls: brand, locale, currency, contact details, delivery/returns rules, image base URL, live API endpoint
switches that turn app behaviour on/off (wire-up required — see README)
brand colours, category colours, glass surface values, radii, font stack
launch screen: logo asset, timing of each animation phase, skip label
every short UI string: nav items, buttons, field labels, placeholders, badges, empty-state text
longer screen copy: hero slides, feature blocks, section headings, notes, error text
the catalogue categories (6 from the website + amazing-deal), their tile art, colours and subcategories
leaf filter chips (e.g. "4 Seater") and the category/subcategory they belong to
deals filter options: minimum discount bands, price bands, sort options
delivery, returns and warranty text; warranty wording is per category
payment methods, flexi-payment split rules and the notes shown at checkout
fulfilment options (home delivery / click & collect), form fields, confirmation copy
showroom list used by checkout and the store screen
sample order records for testing the order-history and warranty UI
sample customer profiles for testing the account screen
the catalogue: 1360 items with prices, badges, stock, delivery, images, sizes, fabrics, colours and specs
the curated deals list: 346 items with their own prices/discounts

assumptions: products comes from the app catalogue feed; 4 live-site slugs that are not in the feed (nice-bookcase, nice-coffee-table, nice-end-table, nice-tv-unit) are excluded.
deals is an independent curated list — an item can appear in both sections with different prices on purpose (the deals screen reads deals).

sizes[].price is the per-size price from the site (authoritative) when sizesFrom is "site-prices"; "site-labels" means the site lists size names only, so every size inherits the product price. A product with a single size step ("Single", "Standard", "6 seater") gets sizeLabel instead of an array — that means there is no size choice to make.
stockCap is the raw stock number the site reports; the "up to N per order" cap shown to customers is settings.commerce.maxPerOrder.
madeToOrder is derived from the description text (that is what the app does today). Once the app reads this file, edit the flag directly.

Some catalogue rows are duplicates or size-sibling rows of each other (11 rows are byte-identical duplicates and are flagged with duplicateOf; a handful more are separate rows that the app folds into one listing card via sizeVariants.ts). The feed is the right place to reconcile those; this file keeps every row so nothing is hidden from you.
Bundled local images (assets/images/**) stay in code because they are module requires, not data; this file carries the remote URLs and relative gallery paths.
Warranty wording is per category today (a hardcoded function in the app) — it now lives in policies.warranty.byCategory.

products._comment: The catalogue. One line per product (see _fields for each key). Set enabled:false to hide an item while testing.

_fields.id: unique id, "<sku-number>-<slug>" — referenced by orders and cart lines
_fields.sku: the storefront SKU, shown on the product page
_fields.name: display name
_fields.subcategory: must match a subcategory id inside that category
_fields.subcategoryName: display name for the subcategory (used in filter chips)
_fields.listPrice: original price for the strike-through; equal to price when there is no discount
_fields.discountPercent: whole percent, used by the "% OFF" pill
_fields.badges: merchandising labels; colours come from labels.badges
_fields.stockStatus: in_stock / out_of_stock / made_to_order (free text as the feed reports it)
_fields.stockCap: raw stock number the feed reports (null when unknown)
_fields.deliveryDays: lead time in days, used by "Delivery in about N days"
_fields.deliveryEstimate: date the site quoted at harvest time (goes stale) or estimated days
_fields.freeDelivery: free delivery applies to this item
_fields.freeAssembly: free assembly applies to this item
_fields.madeToOrder: shows the MADE TO ORDER tag (derived from description today)
_fields.gallery: up to 8 image paths relative to settings.images.baseUrl
_fields.sizeLabel: the single size the item comes in ("Single", "Standard", "6 seater") — no choice to make
_fields.sizes: size choices when the item has more than one — each {label, price, listPrice}
_fields.sizesFrom: where sizes came from: "site-prices" (prices per size) or "site-labels" (labels only)
_fields.fabrics: fabric options shown on the product page
_fields.views: views in the last 24 hrs as the site reported them
_fields.rating: average rating (null when the site has none)
_fields.duplicateOf: id of an identical row — the listing folds these; hide one if you want
